links.outcome: Proportion of fabricated or non-verifiable citations in LLM counselling responses
links.effect: GPT-4 produced the most hallucinated citations (36%) compared with Gemini (14%) and DeepSeek (8.8%) (p < 0.00001).
links.quote: GPT-4 produced the most hallucinated citations (36%) compared with Gemini (14%) and DeepSeek (8.8%) (p < 0.00001).

links.outcome: Readability of LLM patient counselling responses (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease and Grade Level)
links.effect: DeepSeek had the highest readability (FKRE 2.92 (0.27), p < 0.00001). Empathy and readability were negatively correlated (r = -0.34, p = 0.002), suggesting a trade-off between affective tone and accessibility.
links.quote: DeepSeek achieved the highest accuracy (4.77 (0.51), p = 0.0078) and readability (FKRE 2.92 (0.27), p < 0.00001), while Gemini outperformed in empathy (4.08 (0.89), p < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance of three general LLMs (ChatGPT-4, DeepSeek V3, Gemini 2.5 Pro) on standardized patient questions for aesthetic facial surgery across accuracy, empathy, readability, and hallucinated citations without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
